assistant_chosen: Preheat your oven to four hundred fifty degrees Fahrenheit. If using a knife, look for clear, not red or pink, juices running from the spot where you pierced the meat and opaque, barely pink flesh at the bone. If the chicken isn't done, roast for an additional five to ten minutes and check it again. Add eight ounces of fresh chanterelle mushrooms and a pinch of salt, sautéing until the mushrooms release some of their liquid without burning or losing their texture, which should take six to eight minutes. Return the defatted liquid to the pan, cook over high heat, and whisk in one cup of heavy whipping cream, cooking until the liquid thickens slightly. Taste the sauce and season with salt

assistant_chosen: Preheat your oven to three hundred fifty degrees Fahrenheit. Place one cup of chopped pecans on an ungreased baking sheet and toast them until they turn slightly darker and fragrant, which will take about seven minutes; then set them aside. Line baking sheets with parchment paper or silicone liners, or generously grease them with butter or cooking spray. Using an electric mixer fitted with the paddle attachment, beat one pound, or four sticks, of unsalted butter at room temperature with one cup of sugar in a large bowl on medium-high speed until the mixture is light and fluffy, which will take about four minutes. Beat in two large egg yolks and one quarter cup of maple syrup. Add two and three quarter cups of all-purpose flour, one half teaspoon of kosher salt, and one teaspoon of vanilla extract, and beat on low speed until just incorporated. Stir in the toasted pecans. The dough will be soft and somewhat sticky. Divide the dough into two clumps. Set each clump on a long sheet of plastic wrap or waxed paper, shape the dough into two even logs, and wrap them tightly. If you prefer the look of a square cookie, lightly press the logs on four sides to flatten. Refrigerate the dough for at least two hours or overnight. If you are in a hurry, freeze the dough for about twenty minutes, just until it retains its shape when sliced. When ready to bake, unwrap a log of dough and cut it into slices that are one eighth inch thick. Place the slices on the prepared cookie sheet and bake until they turn golden around the edges, which will take ten to twelve minutes. The cookie dough can be made and rolled into logs up to one month in advance and frozen, or up to one week in advance and refrigerated. To prepare frozen dough for baking, remove it from the freezer and set it at room temperature for one hour before baking, or simply transfer the dough from the freezer to the refrigerator the night before baking. Refrigerated dough can be sliced and baked straight from the refrigerator. The baked cookies will keep in an airtight container for up to three days. To make rectangular cookies, form the dough into one rectangular-shaped loaf, wrap it, and refrigerate as directed above, then cut into slices lengthwise and bake.

Using a strainer, extract the boozy Prosecco fruit from the liquid and add it to the custard, stirring gently to combine. Carefully pour the custard and fruit over the bread cubes, distributing the fruit evenly, and let the bread soak along with the custard and fruit for about fifteen to twenty minutes. assistant_chosen: Slice one chicken breast against the grain on the diagonal into pieces that are one centimeter thick. Season the chicken with a pinch of salt and one tablespoon of sake, then coat it with a sprinkle of katakuriko. Rub the salt, sake, and katakuriko into the meat. Bring about one liter of boiling water for every chicken breast you are cooking. Scatter the chicken pieces into the boiling water. When the water is just about to come to a boil, turn the heat down to low. Keep the water just below its boiling point and simmer the chicken for five minutes. Drain the chicken, and it is done. The katakuriko coating gives the chicken a moist, toothsome, tender texture. Be sure to cook the chicken through properly; if the chicken pieces are one centimeter thick, they should be cooked through in five minutes. Make sure to cook the chicken in water that is not quite boiling, as letting the water come to a rolling boil will make the chicken tough and cause the juices to run out. Mix the chicken in the water one to two times during cooking. It is easiest to cook about two to three chicken breasts at a time; just double or triple the amounts of salt, sake, katakuriko, and water. If you do not like chicken that much, marinate it in sake for thirty minutes to an hour after slicing, then salt it and coat it with katakuriko before cooking to get rid of any gaminess.

After chilling, take it out and using either your fingertips or a pastry cutter, break the fat into small pieces until the mixture resembles a crumbly mess. Gradually add either your iced liquor and water mixture or two to three tablespoons of ice water to the mixture, about one tablespoon at a time. Once you can press a handful of the mixture into your fist and it holds its shape, it is ready. Chill the pie crust for three to six hours, or ideally overnight. When ready to roll out, let the crust come to room temperature for a while, then place it on a piece of wax paper and roll it into a circle about ten to eleven inches in diameter. Transfer the crust to a nine-inch pie pan. You can either add a piece of parchment paper with some pie weights or dock the pie, then bake it at three hundred seventy-five degrees Fahrenheit until golden brown, which should take about twenty minutes. After baking, let the pie cool to room temperature while you prepare the filling. For the filling, bring two cups of milk to a simmer in a saucepan. Meanwhile, whisk together six egg yolks, one quarter cup of cornstarch, one half cup of sugar, and one quarter teaspoon of salt until smooth. Slowly add some of the hot milk to the egg mixture, a couple of tablespoons at a time. Once the egg mixture is close to the temperature of the milk and has loosened up, add it all back to the pan. Whisking almost constantly, bring the mixture back up to a simmer and keep it there until it becomes very thick. Remove from heat and slowly add in one half tablespoon of butter and eight ounces of chopped chocolate a little at a time. Let the mixture sit until it is at room temperature or slightly warmer, then spoon it into the shell, smooth it out, and refrigerate until firm. assistant_chosen: Start by dropping one medium sized firm ripe tomato into boiling water for fifteen seconds, then peel off the skin, cut out the stem, and cut the tomato in half crosswise. Squeeze the halves to remove the juice and seeds, then coarsely chop the pulp. Next, roast one and one half pounds of eggplants by pricking them in three or four places, then impaling them on a long handled fork and turning them over a flame until the skin chars and cracks, or by piercing the eggplants, placing them on a baking sheet, and broiling them four inches from the heat for about twenty minutes, turning them so that they char on all sides. After roasting, wrap the eggplants in a damp towel for five minutes, then peel off and discard the skin. Cut the eggplants in half, chop them fine, and mash the pulp to a smooth puree. Similarly, mash the skinned and de-ribbed two medium sized green peppers that have been roasted and peeled. Combine the eggplant and pepper puree in a deep bowl, then stir in one quarter cup of olive oil and three tablespoons of red wine vinegar, adding them a tablespoon at a time, and beat vigorously with a wooden spoon until the mixture is smooth. Add the chopped tomato, three tablespoons of finely chopped fresh parsley, two teaspoons of finely chopped garlic, one tablespoon of salt, and a liberal grinding of fresh ground black pepper, continuing to beat until all the ingredients are well mixed. Taste for seasoning and refrigerate until chilled. Serve mounded on a platter as a first course or spread on dark bread as an accompaniment to drinks.

Pour this mixture over the grated carrots and toss to combine. Let the salad marinate for at least two hours before serving.

assistant_chosen: To make the lattice-top strawberry pie, start by combining two and one half cups of all-purpose flour, two teaspoons of sugar, and two teaspoons of kosher salt in a large bowl. Then, add one half cup of cold unsalted butter, cut into small pieces, and six tablespoons of cold vegetable shortening, rubbing them into the dry ingredients until the mixture resembles coarse meal. Gradually and gently stir in just enough ice water, about six tablespoons, to make the dough come together, then gently press the dough into a ball. Wrap the dough in plastic and refrigerate for thirty minutes. While the dough is chilling, preheat the oven to four hundred twenty-five degrees Fahrenheit. For the filling, toss together three pints of hulled and halved fresh strawberries, three quarters cup of sugar, and six tablespoons of all-purpose flour in a large bowl, then set aside. On a lightly floured surface, roll out half of the dough to fit a nine-inch pie plate, fit the dough into the pie plate, and spoon in the strawberry filling. Scatter one tablespoon of cold unsalted butter, cut into small pieces, evenly over the top. Roll out the remaining dough, cut it into strips that are one half inch wide, and weave a lattice top over the filling. Trim and crimp the edges, then brush one lightly beaten egg over the crust and sprinkle with the remaining tablespoon of sugar. Bake for fifteen minutes, then turn the oven down to three hundred fifty degrees Fahrenheit and continue baking until the crust is nicely browned, which should take about thirty minutes. Once done, place the pie on a rack to cool, then cut into wedges and serve.

To make the filling, preheat the oven to 425 degrees. In a large bowl, toss together 3 pints fresh strawberries, hulled and halved, 3/4 cup sugar and 6 tablespoons all-purpose flour. Set aside. Continue baking until the crust is nicely browned, about 30 minutes. Place on a rack to cool. Cut into wedges and serve.

assistant_chosen: Preheat your oven to one hundred sixty degrees Celsius, or three hundred twenty-five degrees Fahrenheit. Sift seventy-five grams of white flour two or three times. Separate four large egg whites and four large egg yolks. Whip the egg whites to create a meringue, adding fifty grams of sugar in three or four batches, and whip until stiff peaks form, remembering to whip on low speed during the last minute. In a separate bowl, add twenty grams of sugar to the egg yolks in two or three batches and whip until they turn pale and heavy. Mix forty milliliters of vegetable or olive oil, seventy milliliters of water or milk, and a dash of vanilla extract into the egg yolks. Gradually add the sifted flour and mix well. Carefully incorporate the meringue into the egg yolk mixture in two or three batches, mixing gently to avoid popping the delicate bubbles. Pour the batter into the cake dish, gently rapping the pan two or three times against the counter. Bake in the preheated oven for thirty to thirty-five minutes, and do not open the door while baking. Once it’s finished baking, flip the cake upside down and let it cool completely. After it has cooled, insert a knife between the cake dish and the cake, spinning it around once. Use a bamboo skewer to separate the cake from the center part of the mold, and finally, take it out with a knife. The cake should look perfect and is delicious as is, but you can add whipped cream if you like. If the cake makes a puff noise when touched after thirty minutes of baking, bake for an additional five to ten minutes, with a total baking time of around thirty to forty-five minutes.

assistant_chosen: Trim and discard the ends of one pound of long beans, then cut the beans crosswise into segments about one and one half inches long. Heat a wok over high heat until hot, then swirl in two tablespoons of peanut oil to coat the surface evenly. When the oil is hot, stir in six chopped garlic cloves and sauté for a few seconds. Toss in the long beans and stir-fry for one to two minutes. Spoon in two to three tablespoons of roasted chili paste and stir to mix well with the beans. Add a quarter cup of water, stir, and cover with a lid to allow the beans to steam. Open the lid and stir occasionally, adding more water as needed until the beans begin to turn tender. Season to taste with one tablespoon of fish sauce. Add one half to one cup of Thai sweet basil and stir well into the mixture to wilt. Continue to stir-fry until the beans are tender to your liking. Transfer to a serving dish and serve warm along with the other dishes with steamed rice.

assistant_chosen: For the Butter Pecan Donuts, start by adding three tablespoons of active dry yeast, eleven and one half ounces of granulated sugar, forty ounces of cold milk, eighty-six ounces of flour, two tablespoons of salt, four whole eggs, four ounces of egg yolks, and twenty ounces of shortening to a mixing bowl in the order listed. Mix on low speed with a dough hook attachment until the dough is very smooth and elastic, making a slapping sound against the sides of the bowl, which should take about twenty-five to thirty minutes. Scrape the dough into a greased container, cover it, and refrigerate overnight. Two hours before you want to roll the dough, remove it from the refrigerator to temper. Dump the dough onto a floured work surface and roll it to one half inch thick. Cut the donuts using a donut cutter and place them on a tray lined with parchment paper that has been greased and floured. Cover with plastic wrap and let them proof for one hour. Turn on your deep fryer to three hundred twenty-five degrees Fahrenheit. When they are ready to fry, the donuts will feel very light and airy, barely holding their shape when handled. Fry the donuts for two minutes per side, then drain them on a wire rack or paper towels. For the butter crunch, first make the toffee by heating two pounds of butter, thirty ounces of granulated sugar, and one tablespoon of salt in a nonreactive pan on medium-high heat, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon until it reaches a deep golden or caramel color. Pour the mixture onto a silicone baking mat or sprayed parchment paper on a tray and let it cool completely; it will become very hard and shatter if tapped. Next, grind the cooled toffee in a food processor with sixty-two point four ounces of toasted pecans until it is uniformly finely ground. For the glaze, whisk thirty-two ounces of milk with eight and a half pounds of confectioners' sugar together until perfectly smooth, then strain to remove any lumps. To assemble the donuts, dunk the cooled donuts in the glaze and let them drain for one minute before rolling them in the butter crunch, ensuring to completely cover all sides.
